battery_wh.note: Manufacturer states capacity as 48V/30Ah rather than Wh directly; 1440Wh is the derived product (48 x 30), not a value Galbot states verbatim.

locomotion.note: Manufacturer spec table states the chassis is a '4-wheel omnidirectional mobile base' (4轮全向移动底盘); G1 has articulated legs/torso/arms for manipulation but moves on a wheeled base, not by walking -- consistent with the pick-and-place capability entry above and the JD storefront listing.

timeline.detail: First public demonstration of the wheeled mobile-manipulator platform.

The Robot Report reported Galbot deployed at named industrial and healthcare customers (CATL, Bosch, Toyota, Hyundai, Xuanwu Hospital) and running warehouse operations 'for over a year', alongside a new funding round; the article states the company 'claimed that it has secured orders for thousands of units' without independent per-unit delivery evidence (invoice, serial number, unboxing).

source.quote: Galbot's robots are also deployed in multiple warehouse locations, where they've demonstrated stable and continuous 24/7 operations for over a year.
AstraBrain translates natural language into physical actions in real time and supports autonomous task execution without fixed scripts.

review.reason: The text source was reviewed, but no video segment was watched; the existing capability status and autonomy classification for G1 were not fully verified.

capabilities.note: Galbot's own architecture description (via its AstraBrain control stack) explicitly claims autonomous task execution. A public video, 'Galbot G1 pick-and-deliver from shelf to customers 100% automatically!' (YouTube Shorts, https://www.youtube.com/shorts/kb362y4mB9A), shows the shelf-to-customer pick-and-place task referenced here, though a specific in-video timestamp/control statement could not be independently verified during this build. Treated as a manufacturer claim of autonomy for its own control stack rather than an independent-party observation.

order_type.note: Galbot's own G1 page links its 'Buy Now' button directly to a JD.com product listing (item.jd.com/100296074780.html), a live storefront page, rather than a sales-contact form.

notes: No actuator torque figure, SDK open-source/ROS status, or warranty terms for G1 could be pinned to a primary source (galbot.com/g1/ spec table omits joint torque; developer.galbot.com describes a 'GalbotSDK' but does not state an open-source license or ROS/ROS2 support); all three fields left out rather than guessed.

Spec conflict: Galbot's own current Chinese-language product page (galbot.com/g1/, accessed 2026-09-20) states 1730 mm / 92.5 kg / 21 DOF / 8 h runtime / 1.5 m/s max speed / 10 kg combined payload. Widely repeated English-language secondary aggregators (Humanoid.guide, RoboZaps, robotsasia.com, humanoid-robots.io) instead give 173 cm / 85 kg / 47 total DOF (incl. a 12-DOF hand) / 10-hour runtime / 95-97% grasp success rate, none of which trace to a manufacturer page found during this build. Both figures are recorded in this note; the specs above follow the manufacturer's own current page.

https://www.galbot.com/product (the English marketing page linked from search results) returned empty/no renderable content when fetched directly during this build; the specs above come from the manufacturer's Chinese product page (galbot.com/g1/) instead.

The Robot Report (2025-12-23) reports named customers (CATL, Bosch, Toyota, Hyundai, Xuanwu Hospital) and 'Galbot Store' retail deployments in '30+ cities', which is stronger than a bare claim, but the article does not itself supply photo/video evidence of a specific unit, an invoice, a serial number, or a customs record for any single named customer, so delivery.status is kept at 'claimed' rather than 'shipped' or 'demonstrated' per this schema's strict evidentiary bar. This should be revisited if a primary customer case study or unboxing surfaces.
No price was found on a primary manufacturer or press source during this build; price_history is left empty.

Shipped-bar research (2026-09-20): Galbot's own materials and The Robot Report describe G1 running autonomously in pharmacy retail settings ("nearly 10 stores in Beijing") and cite CATL and Bosch as investor/deployment partners, but per our own fetch of the Robot Report piece, no store or partner site is named specifically, and the CATL/Bosch language is about a joint venture and future collaboration, not a documented physical unit in either company's possession with photo plus invoice/serial/unboxing/customs. Not upgraded to shipped.

review.reason: Targeted searches found no confirmed model for this record; does not mean unavailable.
